content:
Maya: Heads-up — seeing ~5-12% UDP packet loss for east-west pod traffic on west2 GPU clusters since the CNI rollout this morning. Affected flows are mainly gRPC over QUIC between training shards. @Alex @Sam

deploy-bot: cni-rollout finished on cluster=west2, version=1.20.0-canary, rollout_id=rl-2026-174523.

Alex: Ugh. Any pattern on MTU / encapsulation? Did we switch encap mode or offload flags in this release?

Maya: Release notes mention ipip -> encap rewrite and a fix for checksum offload handling. I ran a quick `iperf3 -u` between two affected pods:

```
[  5]  0.00-10.00  sec  12.5 MBytes  10.5 Mbits/sec  8.3% loss
[  5]  0.00-10.00  sec  12.5 MBytes  1.05 Mbits/sec   9.9% loss
```

Sam: Can you paste `ethtool -k` from the host NIC and `ip link` inside the pod? Offload mismatch can zero checksums when encap is applied.

Maya: quick snippets:

Host ethtool -k ens192:
```
rx-checksumming: on
tx-checksumming: on
scatter-gather: on
udp-fragmentation-offload: off
```
Pod `ip link` (veth -> gpeer): `MTU 1450`

Kai: 1450 MTU feels like an encap-induced MTU clamp. If encap changed to Geneve/GRE, outer + inner could exceed host MTU and cause fragmentation/loss. But the loss percent being steady suggests offload interaction too.

Nina: We saw similar in canary logs — kernel showed "bad checksum" drops on veth with skb->csum==0 after encapsulation. I can grep kube-proxy/conntrack logs.

Alex: Could also be GSO/GRO toggles. New CNI might be toggling `udp-fragmentation-offload` or `tx-checksum-ipv4` on veths. If the NIC offloads before encap is added, encapsulated pkt carries wrong checksum.

Sam: OK, plan: 1) Enable verbose tcpdump on two pod endpoints for UDP (capture outer+inner). 2) Check host dmesg for skb checksum warnings. 3) If confirmed, rollback west2 canary to 1.19.7 and run canary with `disable_offloads=true` flag.

Maya: tcpdump snippet (outer headers redacted):
```
14:03:12.123456 IP (tos 0x0, ttl 64, id 0) 10.0.1.12.51412 > 10.0.2.8.443: UDP, length 1350
14:03:12.123457 IP (tos 0x0, ttl 64, id 0) 10.0.1.12.51412 > 10.0.2.8.443: UDP, length 200    # inner packet resent
```
Repeated retransmits, inner checksum = 0x0000 in some dumps.

Sam: I'm on it. Starting rollback for canary nodes in west2 now (kubectl set image daemonset/cni cni=1.19.7) — will cordon/drain carefully to preserve training jobs. ETA ~15m.

deploy-bot: rollback job initiated rl-rollback-174523-01, target=west2, target_version=1.19.7.

Alex: While rollback goes, can someone test disabling NIC offloads on one host (`ethtool -K ens192 tx off rx off gso off gro off`) and see if loss disappears? If so, we can push temporary host-level mitigation.

Kai: I'm going to test on one canary host. Will flip offloads and run `iperf3 -u` between two pods on that host.

Nina: Also capturing conntrack counts — if conntrack is seeing too many retransmits we might hit NAT timeouts. Posting logs to the incident thread.

Maya: Thanks — tagging SRE oncall. If rollback doesn't wipe the loss, we'll open an incident and escalate kernel+CNI engineers. For now, mitigation path: rollback + host-offload-disable on affected nodes.

Sam: Rollback finished on 4/6 canary nodes, per deploy-bot. Early metrics show loss down to <1% on those nodes. Continuing with remaining nodes.

deploy-bot: rollback completed on cluster=west2, completed_nodes=6/6, status=success.

Maya: Nice. Loss dropped to noise level on rolled-back nodes. We'll keep monitoring for 2 hours then mark the canary as failed. Filing a bug against the CNI release for `encap+offload` regression with tcpdump evidence.

Alex: Good catch — please add packet captures and host `ethtool -k` outputs to the ticket. We'll coordinate with kernel team if driver interaction suspected. :thumbsup:
